questions.stem: Choose the CORRECTLY spelled word from the options below:

options.option_text: ACCOMODATION (missing one 'm' — should be ACCOMMODATION)
ACCOMMODATION (two c's, two m's — correct spelling)
ACCOMADATION (wrong vowel in second syllable — 'a' instead of 'o')
ACCOMMODASION (wrong ending — 'sion' instead of 'tion')

questions.explanation: B is correct. ACCOMMODATION: AC-COM-MO-DA-TION. Two c's (from ad+com) and two m's (from commodity). This is one of the most commonly misspelled words in English. Memory tip: 'ACCOMMODATION has two c's and two m's — it accommodates them all.'

questions.stem: Identify the INCORRECTLY spelled word in the group:

options.option_text: OCCURRENCE (two c's, two r's — correctly spelled)
PERSISTENCE (correct — from 'persist + ence')
CONSCIENTOUS (should be CONSCIENTIOUS — missing 'i' before 'ous')
BUREAUCRACY (correct spelling — BUREAU + CRACY)

questions.explanation: C is correct — CONSCIENTOUS is misspelled. The correct spelling is CONSCIENTIOUS (CON-SCI-EN-TI-OUS). The word contains 'scienti-' (related to science/conscience) plus '-ous'. The 'i' before 'ous' is commonly dropped in error. All other words are correctly spelled.

options.option_text: SUPERCEDE (wrong — should be SUPERSEDE; there is no 'cede' in this word)
SUPERSEDE (correct — from Latin 'supersedere'; ends in '-sede' not '-cede')
SUPERCEED (double error — wrong middle and wrong ending)
SUPRESEDE (missing first 'e' and wrong prefix letter)

questions.explanation: B is correct. SUPERSEDE is the only English word ending in '-sede' (not '-cede' like precede, concede, recede). This makes it a perennial spelling trap. Etymology: Latin super (above) + sedere (sit) — to sit above, replace. Memory: 'Super + sede — it SITS above all others.'

options.option_text: NECESSARY (one 'c', two 's' — correct: NE-CES-SA-RY)
SEPERATE (misspelling of SEPARATE — 'a' in the middle changes to 'e')
SEPARATE (correct: SEP-A-RATE — 'a' in the middle syllable)
GOVERNMENT (correct: GOVERN-MENT — note the 'n' is present)

questions.explanation: B is correct — SEPERATE is misspelled. The correct spelling is SEPARATE. Mnemonic: 'There is A RAT in SEPARATE' (sepaRATE). This is one of the most frequently confused pairs in English. NECESSARY: one Collar, two Socks (1 c, 2 s).

options.option_text: PRIVILEDGE (incorrect — 'ledge' instead of 'lege')
PRIVELEGE (two 'e' errors — wrong vowels in both syllables)
PRIVILEGE (correct: PRIVI-LEGE — three syllables, ends in '-lege')
PREVILEGE (wrong first vowel — 'e' instead of 'i')

questions.explanation: C is correct. PRIVILEGE: PRI-VI-LEGE. Three syllables. The traps: many add a 'd' (PRIVILEDGE) — wrong; the last syllable is '-lege' not '-ledge'. Etymology: Latin privus (private) + lex/legis (law) — a private law or benefit. No 'd' in the word.

questions.stem: Identify the INCORRECTLY spelled word in the group:

options.option_text: MILLENNIUM (correct: two 'l's, two 'n's — MIL-LEN-NI-UM)
QUESTIONNAIRE (correct: two 'n's — QUESTION-NAIRE)
CALENDER (correct only if referring to a pressing machine; CALENDAR is the scheduling word)
LIASON (should be LIAISON — two 'i's: LI-AI-SON)

questions.explanation: D is correct — LIASON is misspelled. The correct spelling is LIAISON (LI-AI-SON). The word contains two 'i's — a classic error is writing 'LIASON' with only one 'i'. Note: CALENDER (pressing machine) and CALENDAR (date planner) are both correctly spelled as written, so C is not the answer. The unique error here is the missing 'i' in LIAISON.

options.option_text: HARRASS (double 'r' and double 's' — only the 's' is doubled)
HARASS (correct: one 'r', two 's' — HA-RASS)
HARRASE (incorrect ending — 'asse' instead of 'ass')
HARESS (wrong vowel in first syllable — 'e' instead of 'a')

questions.explanation: B is correct. HARASS: HA-RASS — one 'r', two 's'. The most common error is doubling the 'r' (HARRASS). Etymology: from Old French harer (to incite). Memory: 'Don't get stressed — HARASS has one R, two S.' Just like EMBARRASS has two R's and two S's.

options.option_text: ENTREPRENEUR (correct: EN-TRE-PRE-NEUR — note the 'eu' near the end)
BUREAUCRACY (correct: BU-REAU-CRA-CY)
RECIEVE (should be RECEIVE — 'i before e, except after c')
RELINQUISH (correct: RE-LIN-QUISH)

questions.explanation: C is correct — RECIEVE is misspelled. The correct spelling is RECEIVE. Rule: 'i before e, except after c' — RECEIVE follows the 'after c' exception → 'ei' not 'ie'. Other examples: conceive, perceive, deceive, ceiling. Memory: 'CEI-ling and re-CEI-ve — after C comes E-I, not I-E.'

options.option_text: MANAGEABLE (correct: MANAGE + ABLE — the 'e' is retained before '-able')
MANAGABLE (dropped the 'e' before '-able' — wrong for soft 'g')
MANNAGEABLE (doubled the 'n' — wrong)
MANAGIBLE (wrong suffix — '-ible' instead of '-able')

questions.explanation: A is correct. MANAGEABLE retains the silent 'e' from MANAGE because it is needed to preserve the soft 'g' sound (as in 'gem'). Rule: when adding a suffix starting with a vowel (like '-able'), normally drop the silent 'e'. EXCEPTION: if the 'e' is needed to maintain the soft sound of 'c' or 'g', retain it. Compare: MANAGEABLE (soft g preserved), NOTICEABLE (soft c preserved).

questions.stem: Identify the INCORRECTLY spelled word in the group:

options.option_text: INADVERTENT (correct: IN-AD-VER-TENT)
CONSCIENTIOUS (correct: CON-SCI-EN-TI-OUS)
OCASSIONALLY (should be OCCASIONALLY — double 'c', single 's', double 'l')
PERSEVERANCE (correct: PER-SE-VER-ANCE)

questions.explanation: C is correct — OCASSIONALLY is misspelled. The correct spelling is OCCASIONALLY (OC-CA-SION-AL-LY). The errors: only one 'c' instead of two (OC-CA-), and one 's' in '-sion'. Memory: 'OCCASIONALLY has two c's but only one s — like a suit coat with two CC (Casio watch) but one zipper.'

options.option_text: INDISPENSIBLE (wrong suffix — '-ible' not '-able'; INDISPENSABLE ends in '-able')
INDISPENSABLE (correct — IN-DIS-PEN-SA-BLE — ends in '-able' not '-ible')
INDESPENSABLE (wrong vowel in second syllable — 'e' instead of 'i')
INDISPENSEABLE (spurious 'e' inserted before '-able')

questions.explanation: B is correct. INDISPENSABLE: IN-DIS-PEN-SA-BLE. Ends in '-able', not '-ible'. This is a common error. The '-able/-ible' choice: INDISPENSABLE comes from 'dispense' (Latin dispensare); most '-ense'/'-ense' roots take '-able'. Memory: 'INDISPENSABLE — you cannot dispense with the A (in -able).'

options.option_text: ACQUAINTANCE (correct: ACQ-UAIN-TANCE — note the silent 'c' in 'acq')
COMMITTEE (correct: COM-MIT-TEE — double 'm', double 't', double 'e')
MISCHIEVIOUS (should be MISCHIEVOUS — no second 'i' before '-ous')
FLUORESCENT (correct: FLUOR-ES-CENT)

questions.explanation: C is correct — MISCHIEVIOUS is misspelled. The correct spelling is MISCHIEVOUS (MIS-CHIE-VOUS). There is NO extra 'i' before '-ous'. Many writers hypercorrect it as 'mischievious' by analogy with 'devious' or 'previous', but those words have different roots. The word is: MIS + CHIEV + OUS. Memory: 'MISCHIEVOUS is not devious — no extra i.'
